lead: The Web of Things (WoT) gives every device capability a web address and a machine-readable description, so apps can use a sensor or motor like a web resource. A Thing Description (TD) lists properties, actions, events, protocol bindings and security. A servient is the software that serves or consumes TDs and translates web requests to CoAP, MQTT or HTTP. IoT middleware does the same hiding job more broadly: discovery, naming, protocol translation, caching and security mediation. You meet this in smart-home gateways, factory dashboards and city sensor portals, where many devices must look simple to many apps.
prereq: You need: Unit 3 MQTT, CoAP and service discovery, and Chapter 5.2 on cloud platform APIs.

sections.h3: WoT building blocks and the resource model

blocks.text: WoT turns a device capability into a web resource. A temperature sensor may expose /sensors/room1/temperature as a property. A fan may expose /actuators/fan1 as an action. A property is state that can be read and often written. An action is an operation the Thing performs when invoked. An event is a notification, such as an alarm.

The TD is JSON. It gives the Thing an id and title, then lists properties, actions, events, forms and security. A form is a machine-readable link. It states the protocol and URL or topic that reach one capability. The TD is metadata, not the live reading. The reading is the value returned when the resource is read.

The servient can act as client, server or both. A gateway servient runs on a stronger node and exposes many small devices on their behalf. A device servient runs on the device itself, which may be a constrained node.

A protocol binding maps a WoT operation to a concrete protocol. Read property may become an HTTP GET, a CoAP GET, or an MQTT request-reply exchange. The binding lets an app use JSON over HTTP while the device uses CoAP over UDP or MQTT. The resource model stays the same: property, action, event.
IoT middleware is software between applications and devices. It hides hardware and protocol differences. A middleware layer can run at the edge gateway or in the cloud.

items: Discovery finds devices and services. It can use mDNS, DNS-SD or UPnP (discovery in Unit 3).
Naming gives each device and resource a stable name, so an app asks for room1.temperature, not a MAC address.
Protocol translation converts MQTT, CoAP, HTTP or a fieldbus format into one API.
Data aggregation combines readings: average temperature, sum of energy, count of active alarms.
Caching keeps the last value and the TD. An app can read without waking a sleeping device.
Event filtering forwards only useful changes, such as a temperature above a threshold, and drops repeated values.
Security mediation authenticates apps and devices, enforces access rules and terminates TLS or DTLS.

blocks.text: A constrained device has small RAM, a slow CPU and limited energy. Full HTTP over TCP is heavy for it. Many constrained devices use CoAP over UDP, often with 6LoWPAN. A web-enabled constrained device may run a small CoAP server and a compact TD. A gateway servient can translate for devices that cannot run web software. See Chapter 5.4 for the security rules.

Direct MQTT has an app connect to a broker and subscribe to a topic, for example factory/line1/temp. The app must know topic names, payload format and quality-of-service rules. This is simple when both ends are fixed and owned by one team.

WoT adds a description layer. The app fetches a TD and calls a resource. The servient still publishes or subscribes through MQTT. WoT is an abstraction layer over MQTT, CoAP or HTTP, not a replacement.

Benefits are discovery, one API style and self-description. Costs are TD fetch and parse time, an extra servient hop and more metadata. Use direct MQTT for tight control loops with known devices. Use WoT when many apps and devices must interoperate.

A gateway with 20 sensors and 1.2 KB per TD stores 24.0 KB of raw descriptions. A 40% compression leaves 60%, or 14.4 KB. TD size matters on constrained links. Some syllabi treat WoT as a short middleware topic; only a few cover it deeply.

figure.caption: A web client sends HTTP/JSON to a WoT servient. The servient reads the Thing Description and protocol binding to reach the device through CoAP or MQTT.

spec.aria: A web application talks to a WoT servient, which maps Thing Descriptions to CoAP or MQTT and then to the physical device.

examples.question: A gateway exposes 20 sensors as WoT Things. Each Thing Description is 1.2 KB. Compression reduces the stored description size by 40%. Find the total stored size for all descriptions after compression.
steps: Number of Things n = 20. Size per TD s = 1.2 KB.
Raw total = n × s = 20 × 1.2 KB = 24.0 KB.
A 40% reduction leaves 100% − 40% = 60% = 0.60 of the raw size.
examples.answer: The compressed descriptions occupy 14.4 KB; the raw size is 24.0 KB.
examples.check:
n = 20
s = 1.2
total = n * s
compressed = total * (1 - 0.40)
print(round(total, 2))
print(round(compressed, 2))

traps: WoT replaces MQTT or CoAP. It does not; protocol bindings use them.
A Thing Description is live sensor data. It is metadata that says how to reach data.
A 40% reduction means multiply by 0.4. It leaves 60%, so multiply by 0.6.
Middleware is only a broker. It also discovers, names, translates, aggregates, caches, filters and mediates security.
Every constrained device must run a full servient. Many use a gateway servient.

quiz.a: A JSON metadata document that describes a Thing's properties, actions, events, forms, protocol bindings and security.

quiz.q: Why does a WoT system need a servient?
quiz.a: It serves or consumes TDs and translates between the app's HTTP/JSON API and device protocols such as CoAP or MQTT.

quiz.q: A gateway exposes 12 sensors. Each TD is 1.5 KB. Compression saves 30%. Find stored size after compression.
A team adds a new dashboard for 200 devices. Compare direct MQTT with WoT for this change.
quiz.a: Direct MQTT needs every topic and payload known in the dashboard; WoT can discover TDs and use one resource API. WoT adds TD fetch/parse and a servient hop, but reduces coupling.
Any three: discovery, naming, protocol translation, data aggregation, caching, event filtering, security mediation.

quiz.q: Why may a battery-powered sensor not run a full HTTP server?
quiz.a: HTTP over TCP needs more RAM, code and energy; CoAP over UDP or a gateway servient is lighter.

quiz.q: A TD gives a property form with coap:// and the app speaks HTTP. What must the servient do?
quiz.a: Accept the HTTP request, map it through the protocol binding to CoAP, read the device, and return JSON to the app.

quiz.q: Is a TD sensor data? Justify.
quiz.a: No. It is metadata: it says where and how to read data. The sensor data is the value returned by the property resource.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry uses WoT-style device models in digital twins, building automation and industrial asset administration shells. Research extends TDs with semantic vocabularies and composition of Things. Next search terms: W3C Web of Things Thing Description, CoAP Observe, MQTT request-response, digital twin device model. Security work studies capability-based access for servients.
